Dual-point-groups engineering enable multi-ultrahigh-Q resonances via Brillouin zone folding in tetramer metasurfaces
One-shot synthesis of rare gastrointestinal lesions improves diagnostic accuracy and clinical training
articles.abstract: Abstract Rare gastrointestinal lesions are infrequently encountered in routine endoscopy, limiting data for developing reliable artificial intelligence (AI) models and training novice clinicians. Here we present EndoRare, a one-shot, retraining-free generative framework that synthesizes diverse lesion exemplars from a single reference image. Using language-guided concept disentanglement, EndoRare separates pathognomonic lesion features from non-diagnostic attributes, encoding the former into a learnable prototype embedding while varying the latter to ensure diversity. We validate EndoRare across four rare pathologies: calcifying fibrous tumor, juvenile polyposis syndrome, familial adenomatous polyposis, and Peutz-Jeghers syndrome. Experts judge the synthetic images clinically plausible, and data augmentation significantly improves downstream AI classifiers, increasing true positive rates at low false-positive rates. In an exploratory reader study, exposure to EndoRare-generated cases is associated with improved image-level recognition by novice endoscopists. These findings support the potential use of EndoRare as a data-efficient tool for rare-lesion education and motivate prospective controlled validation.

articles.title: Emergence of diffusion models from associative memory through memorization and generalization
articles.abstract: Abstract Dense Associative Memories (DenseAMs) are generalizations of Hopfield networks that store training data at local minima of the energy landscape. When the amount of training data exceeds the critical memory storage capacity, new local minima (different from the training data) emerge. These emergent local minima, known as spurious states, can hinder memory retrieval. We examine diffusion models (DMs) through the DenseAM lens, viewing their generative process as an attempt of a memory retrieval. In the small data regime, DMs create distinct attractors for each training sample, akin to DenseAMs below the critical capacity. As the training set size increases, DMs transition to generalization. We identify a critical intermediate phase, predicted by DenseAM theory, characterized by the emergence of spurious states. In generative modeling, these previously overlooked states are no longer negative artifacts but rather are the first signs of generative capabilities. Their existence is demonstrated across a wide range of architectures and datasets.

articles.title: Complementary axes of functional system integrity and integration with divergent clinical correlates characterize focal epilepsy
Arabian hydroclimate and hominin population dynamics over the last 500,000 years
Structural dynamics of substrate processing by the p97-Ufd1-Npl4-FAF1 machinery
articles.abstract: Abstract The AAA-ATPase VCP/p97 unfolds ubiquitylated proteins in key signaling and cellular homeostasis pathways, yet the mechanisms by which Ufd1-Npl4 and FAF1 adapters handle ubiquitin chains to coordinate substrate loading and processing remain unclear. Our cryo-EM study of p97-Ufd1-Npl4 and FAF1 engaging a substrate reveal interactions that drive substrate processing. While Npl4 is capped by distal ubiquitins, and the initiator ubiquitin can be traced from the Npl4 groove to the ATPase channel at near-atomic resolution, we find that the Npl4 tower adaptively responds to the configurational changes in the ATPase motor’s spiral staircase. A helix in FAF1 together with the Ufd1-UT3 domain engage proximal ubiquitins while providing the necessary structural plasticity to accommodate this motion and deliver ubiquitins to Npl4’s groove. Our study reveals the intricate, dynamic interplay between p97, Ufd1-Npl4, and FAF1 in efficient processing of ubiquitylated substrates.

articles.title: Active locomotion predictively rescues head direction attractor dynamics in head-fixed mice
articles.abstract: Abstract Head direction (HD) cells in the anterodorsal thalamic nucleus form the brain’s internal compass, and are often modeled as a ring attractor maintaining azimuth coding by leveraging continuous visual and inertial sensory input. Here, we test how the common experimental preparation of head-fixed animals alters this code. Complete head-fixation that creates vestibular conflict disrupts both unit and population encoding of head direction, while selectively constraining head-on-body movements either in real or virtual reality uniquely impairs HD population activity. More specifically, attractor dynamics are altered in head-restrained male mice during periods of immobility, and a computational model recapitulates this effect by perturbing lateral connectivity among HD neurons. These dynamics recover several hundred milliseconds prior to locomotion onset, suggesting that an efference copy or prediction of a re-afferent signal is necessary to maintain HD network activity during head restraint. More generally, the results indicate that the HD network is a context- and state-dependent predictive estimator, stabilized by forthcoming self-motion signals. The classic ring-attractor models should be revised to integrate context-dependent dynamics with prospective motor signals, offering a more complete account of how the brain’s compass remains stable across both naturalistic and constrained conditions.

articles.title: Superior energy-storage performance in BaTiO3-based MLCCs via high-entropy driven multiscale optimization
From microstructure to function: spatial visualization of magnetic permeability
Holographic focused ultrasound enables multitarget EV and MSC delivery for neurovascular repair after ischemic stroke
NYNRIN safeguards leukemia stem cells by sustaining thioredoxin activity to maintain redox homeostasis
Programmable roll-to-roll laser processing for high value application of low-grade carbon fiber materials
articles.abstract: Abstract Growing production of carbon fibers generates substantial short-chopped fibers that are difficult for high-value use due to their structural discontinuity. Carbon fiber felts offer potential, yet weak inter-fiber bonding and poor conductivity limit the performance. We report a roll‑to‑roll laser processing strategy that uses a liquid precursor to form laser‑induced graphene at fiber‑fiber interfaces, creating conductive pathways and mechanical interconnections. This approach increases tensile strength from 4.1 to 32.2 MPa and electrical conductivity from 1224.0 to 15151.5 S/m. The resulting films demonstrate efficient electrothermal de‑icing and, after copper deposition, lightning strike protection with a damage area of 9657 mm² and depth of 0.4 mm, comparable to aluminum mesh but with 15% lower weight. A custom‑built laser platform enables scalable production. Here, we show the conversion of low‑grade carbon fibers into lightweight, functional films for aerospace applications via scalable laser processing.

articles.title: Evaluating anonymized genome re-identification using polygenic predictions and its implications for data privacy
articles.abstract: Abstract Re-identification by phenotypic prediction aims to determine whether a genome belongs to a specific individual by comparing the individual’s known traits with those predicted from the genome. Although this tracing attack is widely discussed in the genomic privacy literature, its practical risk remains uncertain. As genome-wide association studies (GWAS) continue to improve phenotypic prediction, concerns about the potential for this attack increase. Here, to quantify its real-world threat, we develop a probabilistic framework that estimates the likelihood of a match between an individual’s observed traits and polygenic scores (PGS) derived from a genome, while accounting for prediction accuracy and genetic and environmental correlations between traits. We benchmark this re-identification method and examine how the prior probability that a random genome and set of traits correspond to the same person affects performance. Finally, we assess whether sensitive genetic information, such as APOE- ε 4 status (linked with Alzheimer’s disease) can be inferred through this attack. Our method outperforms a state-of-the-art tool, reaching a precision above 99% for a recall of 40% when considering a prior of 50%. However, in real-world settings, we estimate that realistic priors do not exceed 4 × 10 −4 %, resulting in a precision lower than 0.13% at the same recall. Inference of sensitive genetic variants also proves ineffective: precision above 50% for identifying APOE- ε 4 carriers is achieved only at a recall below 20%. Thus, although re-identification by phenotypic prediction is technically feasible, its effectiveness in real-world conditions remains limited.

articles.title: A multi-functionally integrated modular catalyst for efficient chemoselective hydrogenation
Structure and function of cyanobacterial Omp85 reveal Toc159/Toc90 as a chloroplast protein import pore
Molecular basis for DNA cleavage by the mini-RNA-guided endonuclease Casδ−1
Spatiotemporal proteomics reveals dynamic antiparallel gradients shaping signalling waves
articles.abstract: Abstract Embryonic development is driven by dynamic protein networks, yet how these dynamics shape morphogenesis remains poorly understood. Somitogenesis, the rhythmic segmentation of vertebrate embryos, is controlled by signalling gradients and oscillations in the presomitic mesoderm (PSM), but the underlying protein dynamics remain largely unknown. Here, we combine microfluidic synchronisation of mouse embryo tails with quantitative proteomics and transcriptomics to resolve spatiotemporal protein dynamics during somitogenesis. We identify proteins with dynamic expression during somitogenesis and reveal an antiparallel, dynamic R-Spondin/LGR signalling pattern that explains how Wnt oscillation amplitude increases despite declining Wnt ligand levels in the anterior PSM. Dynamic ligand expression is validated in mouse gastruloids, and perturbation of ligand dynamics reduces oscillation amplitude and impairs somite formation. Together, our findings identify R-Spondin as a dynamic amplifier of Wnt signalling oscillations and provide a mechanistic framework for understanding how protein dynamics regulate mammalian tissue patterning.

articles.title: The extracellular turret as a structural hub for voltage sensor-pore coupling in HCN channels
articles.abstract: Abstract Hyperpolarization-activated cyclic nucleotide-gated (HCN) channels are essential for rhythmic electrical activity in cardiac and neuronal cells, and their dysfunction underlies disorders such as arrhythmia and epilepsy. Although HCN channels share a conserved six-transmembrane architecture with voltage-gated K⁺ (Kv) channels, how voltage-sensing domains (VSDs) are coupled to pore opening remains incompletely understood. Here, we identify an extracellular pathway that couples voltage-sensor movement to pore opening via the extracellular turret helix, which acts as a critical determinant of voltage-dependent gating in HCN channels. Alanine-scanning mutagenesis of HCN4 revealed six turret residues whose substitution abolished hyperpolarization-evoked currents. Voltage-clamp fluorometry showed that these mutations preserved S4 activation while selectively disrupting turret conformational changes, thereby uncoupling VSD movement from pore opening. Structural and functional analyses further identified an extracellular interaction network linking the turret to the S1, S5, and S6 segments that is essential for hyperpolarization-dependent gating. Collectively, these findings identify the extracellular turret as an active gating hub that coordinates concerted extracellular rearrangements to transmit voltage-sensor displacement to the pore. On the basis of these results, we propose a hand-in-hand coupling model, in which turret rearrangements act as a key downstream relay in the voltage-dependent opening of HCN channels.

articles.title: Unconventional DNA architecture in a dopamine–bound aptamer complex
articles.abstract: Abstract Aptamers are oligonucleotides that have been selected to bind a particular target. Despite the growing popularity of functional DNA aptamers, there remains limited knowledge of their binding mechanisms, as few have been characterized at the atomic level. Here, we use NMR spectroscopy to obtain structural details of RKEC1, a shortened version of a DNA aptamer previously reported to bind dopamine. We find that RKEC1 forms a compact structure upon ligand binding that lacks any Watson-Crick duplex regions or G-quadruplex core, in stark contrast to nearly all predicted and observed DNA aptamer folds. The atomic details explain dopamine specificity amongst structurally similar compounds, and the determined DNA fold was used to guide biosensor design. The aptamer structure further suggests that DNA folding can access an extensive conformational landscape reminiscent of RNA, thus expanding the diversity traditionally captured by predictive algorithms.

articles.title: Structural dynamics between Argonaute-2 and CK1α promote target RNA release in microRNA-mediated silencing
articles.abstract: Abstract Argonaute (Ago) proteins associate with 20-22 nucleotide (nt) long microRNAs (miRNAs) to constitute the functional RISC core and downregulate mRNAs containing complementarity to the seed sequence. Target RNA engagement in RISC stimulates CK1α-mediated phosphorylation of the conserved eukaryotic insertion (EI) in Ago, releasing the target and enabling the RISC complex to suppress additional target sites for efficient miRNA-mediated silencing. Here, we provide a complete structural view of miRNA guide and target binding to human Ago2, showing Ago2 holding the double-stranded guide-target RNA in an untwisted conformation at its center. We visualize the dynamic changes that RISC undergoes as the guide supplementary region progressively base pairs with the target, enabling CK1α binding. Following seed-helix assembly, initial supplementary pairing restricts RISC to a “closed” form, while with half-supplementary pairing, the PAZ domain moves to open RISC to become receptive to CK1α, exhibiting an initial increase in Ago2 phosphorylation. Complete supplementary pairing supports a full PAZ-CK1α interface, allowing for hierarchical phosphorylation of the EI. The combination of target repulsion by EI phosphorylation with an unwound guide-target enables efficient target release to promote RISC turnover.

articles.title:
Electrification,
Lightweighting, and Materials Supply:
A Dynamic Life Cycle Assessment of the U.S. Light-Duty Vehicle Fleet
articles.abstract: Abstract Electrification and lightweighting are reshaping vehicle designs and materials demand, with uncertain net effects on life cycle greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. Most existing fleet studies treat material choices, materials markets, and vehicle adoption separately, without capturing feedbacks between design, supply chains, and consumer behavior. This study develops an integrated system dynamics–life cycle assessment (SD–LCA) framework to explore these interactions for the U.S. light-duty vehicle fleet from 2000 to 2060. The model extends an established powertrain diffusion framework by endogenizing vehicle body material selection, battery capacity evolution, and materials market responses, linking these dynamics to a bottom-up life cycle assessment of fleet GHG emissions. Scenario analysis shows that increasing aluminum use in lightweight gasoline vehicles improves their utility and market share, largely offsetting use-phase GHG savings and yielding only modest reductions in total fleet emissions. In contrast, faster battery electric vehicle adoption raises cradle-to-gate emissions but more than compensates through lower use-phase emissions, reducing total fleet GHGs. Shifts in vehicle material demand also generate transient imbalances in steel and aluminum markets, temporarily lowering recycled fraction and increasing cradle-to-gate emissions. The SD–LCA framework demonstrates how feedbacks between vehicle design, materials supply, and consumer adoption shape fleet decarbonization pathways.

articles.title:
Trihalomethane Exposure,
Seminal Plasma Metabolomics,
and Semen Quality in Healthy Men: A Meet-in-the-Middle Approach
articles.abstract: Abstract Exposure to trihalomethanes (THMs) has been linked to reduced human semen quality, but the critical windows of vulnerability and underlying biological mechanisms remain unclear. We therefore measured untargeted seminal plasma metabolomics to identify metabolic biomarkers and biological pathways linking blood THM concentrations to repeated measurements of semen quality (4146 measurements over a 3 month follow-up period) among 762 healthy Chinese men. We found inverse associations between blood THM concentrations (i.e., chloroform, bromodichloromethane, and chlorinated THMs) and semen volume and total sperm count (all P values <0.05), which were most pronounced for exposure measured 70–90 days prior to semen collection (corresponding to the early stage of spermatogenesis). Metabolome-wide association analyses identified 90 metabolites that were simultaneously associated with blood THM concentrations and sperm-quality parameters. Mediation analyses further revealed that 44 metabolites, enriched in the pathways of unsaturated fatty acid biosynthesis, steroid hormone biosynthesis, arachidonic acid metabolism, linoleic acid metabolism, pantothenate and CoA biosynthesis, and β-alanine metabolism, mediated a considerable proportion (8.1–41.3%) of the inverse relationships between THM exposure and semen quality. Our results suggest that THM exposure during the early stage of spermatogenesis is associated with reduced human semen quality, potentially driven by perturbations in lipid metabolism, steroid hormone synthesis, and antioxidant-related metabolisms.

articles.title:
Relative Humidity
Modulates Nitration and Ring Fragmentation
during Heterogeneous Oxidation of Catechol by Nitrate Radicals
articles.abstract: Abstract Catechol is an important biomass-burning-derived phenolic compound and a precursor to secondary organic aerosols (SOAs). Although nitrate radicals (NO3) are recognized as major nighttime oxidants, the influence of the aerosol water content on heterogeneous NO3 oxidation of phenolic compounds remains poorly understood. Here, we investigate the impact of relative humidity (RH = 0–90%) on the heterogeneous oxidation of catechol thin films by nitrate radicals generated from the reaction of O3 and NO2. Product formation was characterized using Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy, UV–visible spectroscopy, electrospray ionization mass spectrometry (ESI-MS), ultrahigh-pressure liquid chromatography coupled with mass spectrometry (UHPLC–MS), and ion chromatography–mass spectrometry (IC–MS). Under dry conditions, oxidation favored nitration and oligomerization pathways, producing mono-, di-, and trinitrocatechols together with catechol dimers and trimers. These products exhibited enhanced absorption in the 300–500 nm region, characteristic of brown carbon chromophores. Increasing RH progressively suppressed the relative nitration capacity of the NO3/N2O5 system while promoting oxidative ring-opening reactions, leading to the formation of dicarboxylic acids, including cis,cis-muconic acid, 2,3-dihydroxymaleic acid, and oxalic acid. Product distributions revealed a transition from functionalization-dominated chemistry at low RH to fragmentation-dominated chemistry at high RH. These results indicate that RH strongly controls nighttime nitrate radical oxidation of biomass-burning phenolics by shifting product formation from light-absorbing nitroaromatic brown carbon toward highly oxygenated fragmentation products. The findings provide new mechanistic insights into the role of aerosol water in governing the chemical aging and optical evolution of biomass-burning aerosols.

articles.title:
From
Molecular Topography
to Ozone Pollution: Species
Sources and Photochemical Kinetics of Individual Organic Peroxyl Radicals
articles.abstract: Abstract Ground-level ozone (O3) poses significant threats to global public health and climate change. Organic peroxyl radicals (RO2) serve as crucial intermediates in atmospheric O3 formation. Although individual RO2 species exhibit distinct reactivities, the quantification and source attribution of individual RO2 species remain poorly understood. Here, we address the challenge by integrating high-resolution field observations with fundamental theoretical kinetics within a novel hybrid receptor-kinetic modeling framework. The concentration and composition of RO2 species exhibit significant seasonal and diurnal dependencies. In summer, the 19 RO2 pool was characterized by a substantial contribution from biogenic sources (29%), particularly isoprene-derived species (ISOPOBO2). Conversely, the wintertime RO2 composition shifts, dramatically dominated by industrial emissions (41%), notably ethylene-derived species (HOCH2CH2O2). Source apportionment via the RO2+NO pathway further demonstrates that O3 photochemical formation potentials align closely with the kinetics of RO2 production. A data-driven machine learning model effectively captures the contribution of individual RO2 species to O3 formation in summer, but it shows significant deviations from kinetic simulations in winter. The framework establishes a dynamic framework to support daytime O3 mitigation by quantifying the high-time-resolution RO2 radical pool from field VOCs measurements.

articles.title:
Plant
Oxidative Stress Mediates the Synergistic Transformation
of Benzotriazole Ultraviolet Stabilizers in Rhizosphere Soil: Insights
from Dual Exposure Pathways
articles.abstract: Abstract Benzotriazole ultraviolet stabilizers (BUVs) are widespread emerging contaminants in soil. However, their transformation in the rhizosphere and the regulatory effects of plant oxidative stress on rhizosphere remediation remain unclear. The objective of this study was to investigate these effects using molecular simulations and rhizosphere and foliar exposure experiments. The removal efficiency of the four BUVs was 15–46% higher in the rhizosphere of Helianthus annuus than under natural soil degradation. The plant rhizosphere promoted BUV desorption from soil and induced hydroxylation as a specific transformation pathway. Direct rhizosphere exposure triggered oxidative stress and accelerated reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation in soil. Rhizosphere ROS contributed approximately 31.2%–42.7% to BUV transformation. Foliar exposure experiments suggested that plant oxidative stress is an important contributor to rhizosphere ROS generation. Under BUV stress, plant oxidative stress regulated the composition of dissolved organic matter (DOM) and the selective enrichment of bacteria, including Acidobacteriota, Actinomycota, and Bacteroidota. Multivariate correlation network analysis suggested that foliar exposure resulted in more complex interactions among rhizosphere microenvironmental characteristics than did direct rhizosphere exposure. This study provides insights into BUV transformation in the rhizosphere and establishes a framework for plant signal-guided rhizosphere remediation strategies.

articles.title:
Exploring the Influence
of Chemical Exposures on Breast
Cancer Disparities: High-Throughput Transcriptomic Analysis of Normal
Breast Cells from Diverse Donors
articles.abstract: Abstract Racial disparities in the incidence of, and mortality from, aggressive breast cancers are a pressing public health issue. Many factors have been investigated in these inequities; however, the role of toxicant exposures is not well characterized. We and others have identified substantial inequities in chemical biomarker concentrations by race. The goal of this study was to test the hypothesis that exposure to these chemicals is linked to biological changes relevant to aggressive breast cancers, such as dysregulation of the Hallmarks of Cancer. We used high-throughput transcriptomic profiling of normal primary human breast epithelial cells from diverse donors (n = 6) to test the effects of 8 chemicals (cadmium, lead, arsenic, copper, PFNA, BPA, BPS, and p,p’-DDE) with documented exposure disparities by race/ethnicity across 3 concentrations (100 nM, 1 μM, and 10 μM). Across chemicals, we identified that pathways related to cell cycle regulation and protein secretion were commonly affected. Through bioinformatic estimation of cell-type proportions, we found that metals like lead and cadmium induced cell-type shifts, consistent with the dysregulated cellular plasticity cancer hallmark. Lead- and arsenic-response genes were enriched for genes associated with poor breast cancer survival in the Cancer Genome Atlas. Integrating concentration–response modeling and chemical biomonitoring data, BPA, p,p’-DDE, copper, and lead elicited expression changes at concentrations relevant to the US population. Finally, we identified substantial interindividual heterogeneity in response to chemical classes, with heavy metals producing the largest dose-responsive transcriptional effects. These findings highlight the value of high-throughput transcriptomics as a new approach methodology (NAM) in quantifying how common exposures may impact aggressive breast cancer-associated biological processes.

articles.title:
Direct Evidence
for Carbon Monoxide-to-Dioxin Conversion
via Fly-Ash-Catalyzed Sequential Reactions in Incineration Flue Gas
articles.abstract: Abstract The formation of polychlorinated dibenzo-p-dioxins and dibenzofurans (PCDD/Fs) in industrial thermal processes is traditionally attributed to solid carbon precursors via de novo synthesis. Carbon monoxide (CO), despite serving as an operational indicator of incomplete combustion, has not been directly implicated as a molecular carbon source for dioxin generation. Here, we provide definitive experimental and mechanistic evidence that CO can be catalytically converted into dioxins and dioxin-like compounds through a sequential reaction network mediated by fly ash. Using fixed-bed reactors packed with real fly ash, we isolate CO, H2O, and HCl as minimal reactants to reconstruct flue-gas chemistry. Transition metal species (Cu, Fe) in fly ash catalyze CO conversion via a coupled water–gas shift and Fischer–Tropsch-type process, generating a wide spectrum of aliphatic and aromatic hydrocarbons. Concurrently, fly ash mediates HCl oxidation to active Cl2, enabling chlorination of these intermediates into chlorobenzenes and chlorophenols, which subsequently evolve into polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs), polychlorinated naphthalenes (PCNs), and ultimately PCDD/Fs. Notably, Cl4–8DD/F congeners account for >90% of the formed PCDD/Fs, consistent with de novo synthesis signatures. This work establishes a new mechanistic paradigm for dioxin generation and highlights CO emission control as a critical lever for mitigating toxic pollutant generation.

articles.title: No Significant Elimination of Perfluoroctanesulfonate and Other Common Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances by Adult Fathead Minnows, Pimephales promelas
articles.abstract: Abstract Bioaccumulation dynamics of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) remain poorly understood, and kinetic-based information is lacking across environmental gradients, particularly for Cyprinidae, the largest and most diverse fish family. We examined the influences of pH (6.5, 7.5) and salinity (0.3 g/L, 3.0 g/L) on uptake and elimination kinetics of 19 PFAS, which were selected at low concentrations not eliciting standardized adverse outcomes, in the common Cyprinidae, Pimephales promelas. These PFAS consisted of short- and long-chain perfluoroalkyl carboxylic acids (PFCAs) and perfluoroalkyl sulfonates (PFSAs), a sulfonamide, and fluorotelomer sulfonates. Water, whole-body tissue, and plasma were collected over time, and samples were analyzed via liquid chromatography tandem mass spectrometry. Rapid uptake was observed in tissue, reaching pseudo-steady-state conditions within 24–96 h of exposure initiation; uptake rates increased with chain length but were not influenced (p > 0.05) by pH or salinity. During four separate experiments, no significant (p > 0.05) elimination was observed for PFDA, PFDoDA, PFTeDA, total PFOS, PFOSA, and 8:2 FTSA. Kinetic-based bioaccumulation factors (BAFs) increased with chain length for PFCAs and PFSAs, and exceedances of BAF cutoff values were identified. No significant (p > 0.05) elimination of these PFAS indicates that Cyprinidae should be considered during future bioaccumulation studies.

articles.title: Heavy-Duty Diesel Vehicle Deterioration: Impact of Vehicle Age and Emission Control Technology on NO x Emissions
articles.abstract: Abstract This study examines the effect of aging and deterioration on NOx emissions from heavy-duty diesel trucks (HDDTs) with different emission control technologies, including Engine Control only, exhaust gas recirculation (EGR), and selective catalytic reduction (SCR). In-use tailpipe emissions were measured from 12,023 HDDTs from 13 roadside measurement campaigns conducted in California and Utah between 2008 and 2024. Vehicle registration records and the Environmental Protection Agency’s (EPA) engine certification database were used to identify engine NOx control technology. At younger ages, SCR-equipped HDDTs generally emitted significantly less NOx than non-SCR-equipped HDDTs. However, after several years of aging, NOx emissions from SCR-equipped HDDTs were comparable to or exceeded those from non-SCR-equipped HDDTs across locations, engine manufacturers, and engine model years. Although cumulative lifetime emissions from SCR-equipped HDDTs remained lower than non-SCR HDDTs, the reduction in lifetime NOx emissions was substantially smaller than estimated by EPA’s MOtor Vehicle Emission Simulator (MOVES). MOVES predicts an 80% reduction in lifetime NOx emissions from SCR-equipped HDDTs, whereas our estimate is approximately 32%. These findings may indicate that the long-term benefits of SCR for reducing HDDT NOx emissions are smaller than expected and highlight the need for continued emissions monitoring of in-use HDDTs.

articles.title:
Linking Protist-Bacteria
Trophic Interactions to Organic
Matter Chemodiversity: Insights from a Coal Mine Ecological Restoration
Chronosequence
articles.abstract: Abstract Restoring soil biota and dissolved organic matter (DOM) is essential for sustainable ecological restoration of coal mine sites. Protists, as key microbial predators, are recognized as regulators of multiple belowground processes, yet their roles in shaping DOM during ecological restoration remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated a field-scale coal mine ecological restoration chronosequence using vegetation surveys, ultrahigh-resolution Fourier-transform ion cyclotron resonance mass spectrometry (FT-ICR-MS), and high-throughput Illumina sequencing. Restoration increased plant diversity, coverage, and aboveground biomass, which are key resources for soil organic matter inputs. Soil DOM shifted toward more thermodynamically stable compounds, with enhanced chemodiversity during the restoration process. Protistan diversity, particularly of phagotrophic taxa, increased with restoration age, potentially exerting top-down control that increased bacterial diversity but suppressed fungal diversity. Co-occurrence network analysis and random forest modeling revealed that plant biomass was positively linked with phagotrophic diversity, which might influence DOM composition through direct transformation of organic matter (OM) or indirect regulation of bacterial transformation of OM, contributing to the accumulation of recalcitrant molecules with high stability. Together, these findings uncover a previously unrecognized trophic cascade linking protists to DOM chemodiversity at the molecular level, highlighting the importance of integrating protistan regulation into soil ecological restoration strategies for mine sites.

articles.title:
Economic Potential
of Nuclear Power in the Transportation
Sector: Analysis of E-Fuels as An Alternative Fuel for Total
Cost of Ownership and Vehicle Emissions
articles.abstract: Abstract Advanced nuclear reactors could expand U.S. nuclear energy beyond electricity generation into transportation by supplying heat and power for hydrogen and synthetic hydrocarbon fuel production. We evaluated nuclear-enabled hydrogen for fuel cell electric vehicles (FCEVs) and nuclear-derived electro-fuels (e-fuels) for internal combustion engine vehicles (ICEVs) and hybrid vehicles across selected light-, medium-, and heavy-duty classes. Economic performance was assessed using total cost of ownership (TCO), and environmental performance was evaluated using life-cycle emissions. We then estimated carbon abatement costs for alternative fuel/vehicle pathways relative to conventional gasoline and diesel systems. Our findings indicate that conventional ICEVs fueled by gasoline or diesel generally remain the lowest-cost options in 2035. For small sport utility vehicles (SUVs), however, hybrid vehicles using nuclear-based e-fuels and battery electric vehicles (BEVs) with home charging increase TCO modestly relative to gasoline vehicles, while e-fuels achieve the lowest emissions among the alternatives. In long-haul trucking, hydrogen and e-fuels show potential, with marginal TCO increases relative to conventional systems and relatively low abatement costs. Although hydrogen and e-fuels produced with advanced nuclear reactors remain relatively expensive, continued advances in reactors, electrolysis, and fuel synthesis, together with scale economies, could improve competitiveness, diversify transportation fuel options, and reduce emissions.

articles.title:
River
Plastic Retention and Export across Europe
articles.abstract: Abstract Rivers play a central role in the global distribution of plastic pollution. Despite recent research showing that the majority of plastic is not transported to the sea, most plastic transport models have not explicitly included plastic retention in rivers. We propose a new model to quantify micro- and macroplastic retention on land and in rivers, and export toward the sea. Of the 3.55 Mt year–1 of plastics emitted to the environment, only 0.1% of microplastics and 0.5% of macroplastics are exported from the river outlet. This results in 16.8 (15.7–35.1) kt year–1 of microplastic and 3.2 (1.4–12.1) kt year–1 macroplastic export. Rivers store plastic, retaining 68.3 (156.5–350.1) kt year–1 of microplastics (5.3%) and 84.6 (37.2–320.5) kt year–1 of macroplastics (2.5%), while the greatest proportion of plastic remains on land. Although large basin size and high plastic emission to land characterize high absolute micro- and macroplastic retention and export, large basin size is a weaker predictor for high plastic retention and export per capita. By aggregating ranks for plastic export and retention, we provide a new and comprehensive outlook on the most polluting rivers of Europe. This work provides crucial baseline estimates for plastic pollution in light of missing plastic reduction quotas to guide future prioritization and assessment of mitigation actions.

articles.title:
From
Bench-Scale Experiments to Technical Scale-Up:
Rethinking Sorption Research for the Removal of Trace Organic Contaminants
from Water
articles.abstract: Abstract Drinking water, wastewater, and stormwater systems are increasingly challenged by trace organic contaminants (TrOCs), including PFAS, pharmaceuticals, pesticides, and other persistent and highly mobile contaminants that occur at ultralow concentrations in complex water matrices. Sorption-based treatment processes remain central to TrOC removal because they can concentrate dilute contaminants without generating potentially toxic transformation products. However, much of the current sorption literature remains disconnected from the needs of performance prediction and technical scale-up. Equilibrium and kinetic parameters are often derived under simplified laboratory conditions, using empirically fitted models, elevated contaminant concentrations, and/or nonrepresentative water matrices, limiting their physical interpretability and transferability across treatment scenarios. This review critically examines three interconnected areas governing the engineering relevance of sorption data: thermodynamic principles governing sorption equilibria, mechanistic interpretation of sorption kinetics, and the evaluation and transition of novel sorbents to scaled treatment systems. By identifying limitations in prevailing experimental practices and aligning equilibrium characterization, kinetic modeling, and sorbent evaluation with application-relevant conditions, this review provides a framework for generating mechanistically grounded sorption data to support material selection and translate laboratory-derived sorption data into process design parameters for pilot- and full-scale TrOC treatment systems.

articles.title:
Chasing Bubbles:
Toward a Standardized Approach for
Quantifying Methane Ebullition Using Bubble Traps in Streams and Rivers
articles.abstract: Abstract Ebullition transports large quantities of the potent greenhouse gas methane (CH4) from stream sediments into the atmosphere. However, the use of different sampling designs complicates comparisons of CH4 emissions estimates between studies. Here, we present the first systematic review of sampling designs used in the past for assessing fluvial CH4 ebullition rates. In addition, we conducted field experiments to estimate the optimal number of bubble traps and the length of the sampling period, and to assess uncertainties in determining CH4 content in the emitted bubbles. Our results demonstrate considerable spatial variability in bubble fluxes (0–4.8 L m–2 d–1) and CH4 content in the bubbles (0.01–67%), necessitating a larger number of bubble traps than typically deployed in streams. Using fewer traps leads to greater deviations in CH4 ebullition estimates than shorter deployment times. Therefore, the robust sampling design should account for strong small-scale heterogeneity in streams through an adequate number of bubble traps and link bubble fluxes to trap-specific gas content. It should also consider the risk of CH4 concentration decreases in accumulated bubbles over a few days, primarily due to redissolution, followed by oxidation and leakage.

articles.title:
Evaluating
Emergency
Emission Controls During an Unprecedented
Regional Haze Event Using Causal Machine Learning
articles.abstract: Abstract Emergency emission controls are widely implemented to mitigate severe haze, yet their effectiveness is difficult to disentangle from meteorological variability and concurrent changes in activities. Here, we develop a three-step evaluation approach integrating air quality meteorological normalization, augmented synthetic control, and machine-learning prediction to causally quantify intervention-attributable changes in local emission strength and ambient pollutant concentrations. Applied to Shijiazhuang’s unprecedented 45-day “Sharp Sword to Cut Haze” campaign in 2016, the approach revealed that local emission strengths of PM2.5, PM10, SO2, NO2, and CO were reduced by 4.3%, 4.8%, 15.8%, 5.8%, and 15.3%, respectively. Corresponding concentrations fell by 42.1 (14.8%), 47.4 (12.4%), 13.8 (16.6%), 15.8 (15.5%) μg·m–3, and 0.9 mg·m–3 (19.6%). Observation-based PM2.5 source apportionment results independently supported these estimates: contributions from vehicle emissions, steelmaking, and coal combustion were 4.1%, 11.0%, and 21.7% lower, respectively, than during the corresponding period in 2017. Despite stringent controls, PM2.5 averaged 243.2 μg·m–3 during the intervention period. Thus, stringent local controls substantially reduced emissions, but regional transport and unfavorable meteorology partly offset the resulting air quality benefits, highlighting the need for coordinated regional mitigation.

articles.title:
Multi-Scale Multi-Indicator
Assessment of Material
Recovery Pathways: The Case of the United States Flat Glass Sector
articles.abstract: Abstract Material recovery and circularity analysis offers critical insights for understanding future scenarios and informing strategic decisions toward resource use. However, existing approaches often lack the granularity and breadth needed to capture supply chain dynamics and economy-wide impacts simultaneously. We introduce a novel quantitative framework─Supply Chain Operations Research through Physical Input-Output (SCORPIO)─that addresses this gap by enabling multi-scale assessment of material recovery strategies across both supply chain and macroeconomic levels. To demonstrate SCORPIO’s capabilities, we apply it to flat glass flows in the United States, examining waste valorization practices, including open- and closed-loop recycling. By assessing economic, workforce, and environmental indicators, SCORPIO reveals the potential outcomes and trade-offs of different waste valorization solutions in a holistic manner. Results show that both open-loop and closed-loop recycling of glass from utility solar and commercial buildings have the potential for positive economic impacts at the supply chain and economy level. However, the effect on environmental impacts was less certain, with open-loop recycling generally performing better than closed-loop pathways. This case study illustrates how the SCORPIO framework can support stakeholders navigating the transition toward increased material recovery, offering a methodological foundation applicable to other material systems facing environmental and resource challenges.

articles.title:
Winter and Summer
Differences in Oxylipin Responses
to Ambient Particles: Roles of Sizes and Constituents
articles.abstract: Abstract Ambient fine particulate matter (PM2.5) has been associated with increased mortality risk, but whether it is more harmful on colder or warmer days is unclear. Here, we investigate seasonal variations in PM2.5 mass, sizes, constituents, and their association with oxylipin changes in humans. In a panel study of 123 adults in Beijing, we measured 27 PM2.5 metrics and five circulating lipoxygenase-derived oxylipins (i.e., leukotriene B4 [LTB4], 5-, 8-, 12-, and 15-hydroxyeicosatetraenoic acid [HETE]) across winter and summer. PM2.5 exposure was associated with peak oxylipin increases at lag 0–1 days. Across particle size fractions and constituents, oxylipin increases ranged from 3.3% to 114.2%, with the most robust associations for ultrafine particles, accumulation mode particles, organic carbon, and chloride. Furthermore, an exposure-response relationship between UFP and oxylipins was observed only in summer. An IQR increase in UFP was associated with oxylipin changes of 12.9–97.7% in summer and −7.7 to 18.8% in winter. Conversely, oxylipin increases associated with accumulation mode particles and organic carbon were greater in winter. These findings suggest that the sizes and constituents of PM2.5 may partially explain the seasonal difference in the health effect of PM2.5 exposure, helping identify components associated with stronger biomarker responses in specific seasons.

articles.title:
Phage-Based Biofilm
Control in Engineered Water Environments
articles.abstract: Abstract Biofilms represent a predominant bacterial lifestyle and contribute to the ecological stability and biochemical functioning in water systems. Paradoxically, excessive biofilm formation threatens water security and public health by causing biofouling, harboring pathogens, and facilitating the transmission of antimicrobial resistance. Phage treatment offers a promising strategy for the targeted regulation of biofilm microecology without generating harmful disinfection byproducts. However, its performance in environmental settings can be constrained by spatiotemporal heterogeneity, suboptimal phage exposure, and the evolution of phage resistance in bacteria, creating additional challenges for engineering applications. Here, we synthesize phage-based biofilm control as a multilevel intervention paradigm organized by biological bottlenecks. We examine strategies that improve transport and host access, enhance targeting and productive lysis, induce biofilm disruption through prophage activation, and perturb biofilm communities through keystone-centered interactions. We then align these intervention principles with distinct biofilm scenarios and operational constraints in engineered water environments. Emerging technologies are evaluated according to their roles in target identification, validation under application-relevant conditions, and treatment monitoring. Finally, we propose a closed-loop framework encompassing system diagnosis, intervention design and validation, monitored deployment, and adaptive management. Overall, this Review provides an integrated roadmap for advancing scalable and sustainable phage-based biofilm control in engineered water environments.

articles.title:
Convergent Biogenic
Magnetite Formation from Diverse
Iron (Oxyhydr)oxide Precursors Drives Cr(VI) Reduction via an Environmental
Battery Mechanism
articles.abstract: Abstract Iron (oxyhydr)oxides mediate electron flux across coupled biogeochemical cycles in anoxic environments, yet whether their biogenic transformation feeds back to reshape interfacial electron transfer efficiency remains unresolved. Here, five structurally distinct iron (oxyhydr)oxide precursors (ferrihydrite, goethite, magnetite, wüstite, and hematite) were exposed to anaerobic sulfur-oxidizing bioreactors under Cr(VI) stress, and their transformation trajectories were tracked using synchrotron EXAFS spectroscopy, electrochemical impedance spectroscopy, DFT calculations, and metagenomic profiling. Mineral bioavailability decreased in the order ferrihydrite > goethite > magnetite > wüstite > hematite, a hierarchy governed by lattice iron-leaching energetics quantified via DFT (Efev from −8.96 eV for ferrihydrite to 5.76 eV for hematite). Despite this wide disparity in precursor lability, all biotransformation trajectories converged on magnetite as the thermodynamically stable end point. In the ferrihydrite system, biogenic magnetite reached 60% of the final solid phase and operated as an in situ “environmental battery” (storing and releasing electrons through reversible Fe(II)/Fe(III) lattice cycling), lowering interfacial charge transfer resistance and producing a 4.77-fold higher pseudo-first-order Cr(VI) reduction rate constant than the mineral-free biotic control (C-S). Metagenomic analysis revealed mineral-specific restructuring of the microbial community toward a tightly coupled sulfur–iron redox network. These results reframe precursor mineralogy from a determinant of intrinsic reactivity to a kinetic regulator of biogenic electron-buffer formation, providing a mechanistic basis for mineral-informed bioremediation design.

articles.title:
Post-Regulation
of Nitrogen Configurations in Nitrogen-Doped
Carbon Electrodes for Enhanced Capacitive Deionization
articles.abstract: Abstract Nitrogen doping is widely used to enhance the electrochemical performance of carbon materials, yet its effectiveness is often limited by electrochemically inactive or inaccessible nitrogen configurations. Here, we develop a coupling-agent-mediated amidation strategy to postregulate nitrogen-doped carbon, selectively enriching amino nitrogen while tailoring the distribution of pyridinic, pyrrolic, and graphitic nitrogen. The introduced −NH2 groups elevate the surface charge density, which is favorable for ion adsorption and diffusion. Density functional theory calculations, together with electrochemical kinetic analyses, reveal that edge-type nitrogen, particularly the lone electron pairs on amino nitrogen, can strongly interact with salt ions, resulting in effective electrical-double-layer compression and shortened ion diffusion distance. Consequently, the optimized electrode achieves a specific adsorption capacity of 70.3 mgNaCl g–1 and a time-averaged adsorption rate of 2.3 mgNaCl g–1 min–1 in 1000 mg L–1 NaCl solution at a cell voltage of 1.6 V. Its electrosorption behavior toward monovalent and divalent cations is also systematically evaluated in synthetic brines and actual industrial recirculating cooling water. This study provides a facile, powerful strategy to rationally design carbon electrodes for high-performance electrochemical ion storage and separation applications.
